title: I started building a news app when I was a teenager because I was tired of missing the stories that actually mattered to me.
body:
It wasn't about wanting to be a founder. It was about solving a frustration. Every day I felt like I was drowning in noise and headlines that were designed to make me click rather than think. I wanted news that felt like it was curated for my specific interests, not just a generic feed of whatever was trending globally.

Building Headlinne meant teaching AI to do something very human. It had to learn how to filter out the fluff and find the signal in the noise. The challenge wasn't just technical. It was about respecting the reader's time. If an algorithm is going to suggest a story, it needs to be because that story adds value to the reader's day, not because it hits a metric.

We are now at a point where AI can actually handle the heavy lifting of personalization without losing the nuance of good journalism. It turns out that when you treat readers like intelligent people who want to stay informed, they appreciate it. We aren't trying to change how people consume news. We are trying to make it worth their time again.
cta: If you want to see how we are rethinking the daily feed, you can take it for a spin at HEADLINNE.com.
